content.user_title: Coordinate Interface Animations With Clear Timelines
content.value_statement: Independent animations can create delays, competing movement, and broken transitions. Choreograph guides coordinated timing, reduced-motion alternatives, and interruption handling through CSS and Motion recipes.
actual_capabilities: Assign lead, support, decoration, and static roles to elements involved in an interaction.
Produce timelines showing each element's start, duration, motion, and relationship to other elements.
Provide CSS and Motion recipes for staggered entrances, simultaneous exits, crossfades, and direction-aware steps.
Coordinate container resizing with content transitions and adapt fade duration to height changes.
Guide cancellation, completion tracking, and idle-loop coordination for interrupted animation sequences.
Define reduced-motion alternatives that remove movement and delays while preserving visible state changes.
limitations: Contains written guidance and illustrative recipes, not a standalone animation runtime or automated testing tool.
Motion recipes require a compatible React setup; the resizing example also uses react-use-measure.
Visual quality requires recordings and manual inspection; source code alone cannot establish the final result.
Focuses on relationships between animations, not comprehensive tuning of individual animation easing or duration.

use_cases.title: Simplify Repeated Product Interactions
use_cases.description: Remove nested entrances and unnecessary staggering from menus, drawers, and frequently opened panels.

use_cases.title: Plan First-Visit Entrances
use_cases.description: Assign visual roles and overlapping timing to titles, supporting text, and actions without moving every element.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Step Transitions
use_cases.description: Align navigation direction, container resizing, content exits, and interruption checks across a multi-step interface.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Panel Entrance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the entrance animation in [component]. Identify redundant movement and provide a timeline, static elements, and recording checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Overlapping Entrance
prompt_templates.prompt: Choreograph the first-visit entrance in [page]. Assign element roles, vary support timing, and include reduced-motion behavior without animating the parent entrance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: coordinate a small group of elements.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Direction-Aware Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Update [step component] with Motion transitions that follow Next and Back direction. Coordinate resizing, preserve stable keys, and check rapid repeated navigation.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate Interruptible Interaction States
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [interactive component] across hover, click, reset, and idle states. Coordinate animation cancellation, await reset completion, and specify reduced-motion behavior and interruption tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate several events and animation phases.

output_examples.input: A drawer slides in, then staggers eight menu items. Make it faster to use.
output: Timeline: Drawer is the lead; start at 0ms and complete a single slide in 250ms.
Static elements: Menu rows and action buttons remain inside the drawer without separate entrances.
Feel check: Inspect the opening frames and confirm visible actions respond immediately.

output_examples.input: Removing a tag leaves a gap until its fade finishes.
output: Timeline: The removed tag fades while its siblings move into the gap, starting together at 0ms.
Implementation choice: Use Motion popLayout so the exiting tag stops occupying layout space immediately.
Feel check: Remove several tags quickly and confirm gaps close without waiting for previous exits.

output_examples.input: A step form slides in the same direction for Next and Back.
output: Direction: Next content enters from the right; Back content enters from the left.
State handling: Pass the current direction to both AnimatePresence and its keyed child.
Feel check: Reverse direction mid-transition and inspect for duplicate views or stale exit directions.

best_practices: Inventory moving elements and assign roles before selecting timing or implementation tools.
Use the lightest animation approach and remove staggering from frequently used or keyboard-triggered interfaces.
Inspect recordings, test rapid interruptions, and verify reduced-motion behavior before accepting the choreography.
anti_patterns: Animating a container entrance and then separately staggering all its children.
Applying identical timing and movement to every element, including decorative details.
Starting new sequences without stopping existing animations or waiting for resets to finish.

faq.question: What does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It coordinates relationships between animations, including ordering, overlap, shared timing, exits, and intentional stillness.

faq.question: Does every interaction need a stagger?
faq.answer: No. Frequently used menus, command palettes, and keyboard-triggered interfaces should show items together or avoid animation.

faq.question: Which implementation tools are covered?
faq.answer: The recipes cover CSS keyframes, Motion variants, AnimatePresence, shared layout animation, and imperative useAnimate orchestration.

faq.question: How does it handle reduced-motion preferences?
faq.answer: It removes movement and delays, keeps opacity changes, and shows groups together. Explanatory sequences use discrete frames instead of animated transitions.

faq.question: Can it verify the visual result from code alone?
faq.answer: No. It requests recordings, frame inspection, and interruption checks to evaluate timing and visual continuity.

faq.question: Is this a complete animation library?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example patterns that require integration, compatible dependencies, and testing in the target interface.
